ancestry_summary.statement_nl: Let $n$ be an integer greater than 1. For which real numbers $x$ is \\[\\lfloor nx \\rfloor - \\sum_{k=1}^{n} \\frac{\\lfloor kx \\rfloor}{k}\\] maximal, and what is the maximal value that this expression can take?

payload.proof_nl:
Let d = x - j/n. Since x \ge j/n, subtracting j/n from both sides gives d \ge 0. Also, since x < (j+1)/n = j/n + 1/n, subtracting j/n gives d < 1/n. Hence 0 \le d < 1/n.

By the definition of d, we have x = j/n + d. Since J_{n,j}(d) is defined to be j/n + d, it follows that x = J_{n,j}(d).

This proves the statement.
